t: The Five Dysfunctions of a Team
pitch: A business fable and a simple pyramid: trust, conflict, commitment, accountability, results.
center: The five dysfunctions of a team
br: When someone isn't a team player
quiz: Which dysfunction is at the base of the pyramid?
Without trust based on vulnerability, none of the higher levels can be built.
What kind of trust does Lencioni mean?
Knowing a colleague will meet deadlines
Daring to be vulnerable: saying “I was wrong”, “I need help”
It is the confidence that others have good intentions and that being yourself carries no risk.
Calm, polite meetings where real disagreements are never voiced
Disagreements exist but move to the hallways; decisions are not truly supported.
What are the two obstacles to commitment?
The desire for consensus and the need for certainty
You don't need to win to support a decision, and an imperfect decision beats no decision.
What is the “cascading message” exercise for?
Checking at the end of a meeting that everyone understood the same decision and will pass on the same message
It immediately reveals different interpretations of the same decision.
Who should hold team members to their commitments in a high-performing team?
Peer pressure is the fastest and most effective way to maintain high standards.
The leadership team they belong to with their peers
Their primary loyalty must go to the leadership team, otherwise everyone defends their silo.
What does Kathryn do with the marketing head who refuses to be a team player?
Says nothing to keep her talent
After frank conversations, asks her to leave the company
A brilliant person who persistently refuses to play as a team can stop the whole team from improving.
